title: Read the bone clock
hook: A bone has an eighth of its carbon-14 left. How old is it?

knows: that a half-life is the time for half of the radioactive atoms to decay (the half-life lesson)
doesNotKnow: how to run a half-life backwards to get an age

misconception: A bone with 1/8 of its carbon-14 left is 8 half-lives old (or the age is the missing percentage times something).
objective: The learner can date a sample by counting how many halvings give the remaining fraction (1/8 = three halvings) and multiplying by the half-life: 3 x 5,700 = about 17,000 years.

claims.text: Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,700 years: the time for half of it to disappear.
claims.source: NUBASE2020: Kondev et al., Chinese Physics C 45 (2021) 030001, 14C half-life 5,700 ± 30 y. (Older value 5,730 ± 40 y, Godwin 1962; radiocarbon labs still report 'conventional ages' with the Libby value 5,568 y.) | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 13): NUBASE2020 (Kondev et al. 2021) lists 14C t1/2 = 5,700(30) y; "about 5,700" correct.

claims.text: The fraction of carbon-14 left after time t is (1/2)^(t / half-life).
claims.source: Exponential decay law, N/N0 = (1/2)^(t/T½); any nuclear or physical chemistry text, e.g. Krane, Introductory Nuclear Physics (1988), ch. 6.

claims.text: 1/2 is left at 5,700 years, 1/4 at 11,400 years and 1/8 at 17,100 years: 1/8 is three half-lives, not eight.
claims.source: 1/8 = (1/2)^3, so t = 3 x 5,700 = 17,100 y; 1 x 5,700 and 2 x 5,700 = 11,400 for the other pins. 8 x 5,700 = 45,600 (about 46,000) is the wrong-option slip.

claims.text: After about nine half-lives, roughly 50,000 years, only 1/512 of the carbon-14 is left, too little to measure well; this is about the practical limit of radiocarbon dating.
claims.source: (1/2)^9 = 1/512 at 9 x 5,700 = 51,300 y (derivation). Practical limit about 50,000 years: Hajdas et al., 'Radiocarbon dating', Nature Reviews Methods Primers 1 (2021) 62.

claims.text: The dating assumes the bone started with the same carbon-14 share as the living world and stopped taking in carbon at death.
claims.source: Implicit in 'original carbon-14' in the prediction. Hajdas et al. 2021 (above) on the premise and on calibration, which corrects for past changes in atmospheric 14C. Not shown on the stage; recorded so the simplification is on file.

recall.question: A sample has 1/4 of its original carbon-14 left. With a half-life of about 5,700 years, about how old is it?
recall.why: 1/4 is two halvings (1/2 x 1/2), so two half-lives: 2 x 5,700 = 11,400 years.
